title: Add support to parse general triclinic boxes in `read_lammps_data`, `read_lammps_dump_text`, and `read_lammps_dump_binary`
body:
Closes #1723 

Since the [Feature release 17 April 2024](https://github.com/lammps/lammps/releases/tag/patch_17Apr2024), LAMMPS supports parsing general triclinic boxes, as done in most periodic DFT codes.
This MR adds supports for parsing the general triclinic boxes in `read_lammps_data`, `read_lammps_dump_text`, and `read_lammps_dump_binary`.

The substantial changes are as follows:

- 39bc5945a843160f13e02e263b43b3694ffd7da7: Support in `read_lammps_data`
- 986f52c06c13a5c676fa23994a536a5ed6c7c8de: Support in `read_lammps_dump_text`
- 994a27b6a7fe6fdaaba4d011b8bafb7b73b65875: Support in `read_lammps_dump_binary`

Tests are added for `read_lammps_data` and `read_lammps_dump_text`. For `read_lammps_dump_binary`, it may be a bit challenging to prepare binary files for testing, and indeed now this function is tested only via `LAMMPS` calculator. At least the existing tests are passed, and I checked locally the modified code could parse my small test case.

Taking this opportunity some relevant files are formatted with Ruff.

We can in principle also support writing general tricilinic boxes in `write_lammps_data`. This however requires a new argument to control it and a bit larger modification for handling vector-property rotations, so I would like to separate it into another MR.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body:
I'm not a LAMMPS expert, but the implementation seems fine and the formatting changes also look innocuous. I made some very minor comments/suggestions.

I do wonder if mypy will really be happy working with this `dict[str, float 
| list[float]]`. A stricter implementation with one or two TypedDict is possible. But a lot more verbose and mypy seems quiet on the matter _for now_... So maybe we deal with that problem as it arises :sweat_smile:

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @ajjackson for the review! In the new commit I addressed your suggestions accordingly.

I also agree on the potential concern about `dict[str, float  | list[float]]`. Just now I played a bit with `TypedDict` and `dataclass` but found it a bit cumbersome to keep conciseness. For example, now I use `abc origin` as a key, but for this we need some adjustment for the whitespace in both `TypedDict` and `dataclass`. Since the `box` is a small placeholder used mainly only in the new private `_make_cell` method (which is thus easy to fix), I would suggest leaving it for now.

comments.author: ajjackson
comments.body: I agree. As it exists in this parser the data should not be used too many different ways in practice. A more rigid structure would be nice but not really worth the effort at this moment compared with other work on ASE.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you Adam! I would then like to merge now:)
